name: Chiltepec Chinantec
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.verdict: a source was named but could not be reached
earlier_scan.source_named: Weitlaner, Roberto J. 1947. The Phonemic System of Chinantec, dialect of Chiltepec, Oaxaca. 27th Int. Congress of Americanists Actas vol 2: 313-321. Print only; not found online.

sources.citation: Silverman, Daniel. 2006. Chinantec: Phonology. In K. Brown (ed.), Encyclopedia of Language and Linguistics, 2nd ed., 211-213. Elsevier. (already held under coma1246)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only; lists Chiltepec among the 14 Chinantecan languages, then: 'Stem complexes are obligatorily stressed. Post-tonic and pre-tonic syllables are not stressed.' plus ballistic vs controlled stress on stem syllables. No Chiltepec-specific statement.

sources.citation: Anderson, Judi Lynn, Isaac H. Martínez & Wanda Pace. 1990. Comaltepec Chinantec tone. In Merrifield & Rensch (eds.), Syllables, tone, and verb paradigms (Studies in Chinantec Languages 4), 3-20. (already held under coma1246)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Comaltepec, not Chiltepec. p.4: 'A Chinantec word consists of one or more syllables, only one of which is stressed—usually the last.' Two kinds of word stress, ballistic and controlled.

sources.citation: Thelin, Anders. 1980. Tlacoatzintepec Chinantec syllable structure. SIL-Mexico Workpapers 4: 1-8. [sister variety: Tlacoatzintepec Chinantec, ctl, tlac1240]
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: NOT Chiltepec Chinantec. p.1: 'The rhythm group consists of one to three syllables; only the last is stressed. The bulk of the language corpus consists of rhythm groups with only one syllable.' Sec. 3 (p.5): syllables are ballistic (acute accent) vs controlled. fn.1: the Tlacoatzintepec lect is also spoken by migrants in the town of Chiltepec (migration c. 1930).

sources.citation: Robbins, Frank E. 1961. Quiotepec Chinantec syllable patterning. IJAL 27(3): 237-250 (archive.org scanned of IJAL 27(3)).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: About Quiotepec, not Chiltepec. p.237: 'Weitlaner (1947) reported the phonemes of the Chiltepec dialect, and descriptions of the phonemes of other dialects are in progress'; fn.2 gives the full Weitlaner 1947 reference. No statement about Chiltepec stress.

sources.citation: Weitlaner, Roberto J. & Carlo Antonio Castro G. 1954. Papeles de la Chinantla I: Mayultianguis y Tlacoatzintepec (Serie Científica 3), with H. F. Cline's edition/notes on Barreda 1730. México: Museo Nacional de Antropología (archive.org scanned).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Chiltepec stress. Cline's notes (pp.71, 119-123) identify Weitlaner 1939 'Los chinantecos' (RMEA 3: 195-216, linguistic part pp.205-216, Chiltepec data) as the fullest published sketch and summarise its verb morphology only; p.72 remarks only that Barreda was aware of 'tono o acento' distinguishing homonyms (18th-c. Yólox Chinantec).

sources.citation: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano / SIL Mexico language-survey materials for Chinanteco de Chiltepec [csa] (wordlists, intelligibility survey underlying Ethnologue/Merrifield 1994 classification).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: SIL never ran a Chiltepec program (old SIL-Mexico site has pages only for Comaltepec, Ozumacín, Lealao, Sochiapam, Tlatepuzco, Usila); any unpublished survey transcription would be the only other first-hand Chiltepec material. Could not check OLAC/SIL archive listings for csa today (OLAC unreachable, sil.org 403).

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 1989. An etymological dictionary of the Chinantec languages (Studies in Chinantec Languages 1; SIL Publications in Linguistics 87). Dallas: SIL & University of Texas at Arlington.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Chiltepec is one of the 14 Chinantec languages sampled (the list Silverman 2006 reproduces); the introduction gives per-language phonological conventions (tone, ballistic stress, syllable) and is the only modern SIL source with systematic Chiltepec data.

sources.citation: Rensch, Calvin R. 1968. Proto Chinantec phonology (Papeles de la Chinantla VI; Serie Científica 10). México: Museo Nacional de Antropología / INAH.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Comparative Chinantec phonology with dialect-by-dialect phoneme/prosody summaries; if Chiltepec is in the sample it would give a second-hand stress/ballistic statement with Rensch's own field data.

sources.note: The only published phonemic description of Chiltepec Chinantec (Glottolog's sole descriptive ref; cited as such by Robbins 1961:237). Nine pages; will contain whatever is said about tone/stress/syllable prosody for this lect.

sources.citation: Weitlaner, Roberto J. 1939. Los chinantecos. Revista Mexicana de Estudios Antropológicos 3(3): 195-216 (linguistic sketch pp. 205-216).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Cline (Papeles de la Chinantla I, pp.71, 119) calls it the most complete published description of Chinantec at the time; based on Weitlaner's Chiltepec fieldwork; may contain remarks on accent/tone predating the 1947 phonemic paper.
